# PR #2854: Patch: spec check reads the edge worker's ruling citations too

Closes #2828

## What changed and why

`cargo jackioh spec check` walked only `crates`, `apps/web/src` and `e2e` for ruling citations, so the `R190` comment in `apps/edge/src/routing.ts` and the two `R190` test titles in `apps/edge/src/routing.test.ts` were unchecked in both directions: a mistyped R-id there passed silently, and the README said an edge test could never count as a proof. The check now reads `apps/edge/src` too, and the README documents exactly that. No game behavior changes.

- [spec.rs](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2828/crates/tools/src/spec.rs): `CITING_ROOTS` gains `"apps/edge/src"`; new unit test `check_reads_edge_workers_citations` pins that a valid edge citation passes, a bogus R-id under `apps/edge/src` fails the check, restoring the valid text passes again, and an edge TS title counts as a proof via `proves()`.
- [spec/README.md](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2828/spec/README.md): the proving-test sentence now lists `apps/web/`, `apps/edge/src/` and `e2e/`; the `spec check` paragraph lists all four citing roots and says "those four trees".

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools check_reads_edge_workers_citations` — pass; full `cargo test -p jackioh-tools spec::` — 28 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- Full-tree check with the new code (debug binary): `spec check: 1625 rulings, 3848 proofs, 47616 citations in 3105 files, 20634 links: ok` — the +9 citations/+2 files over baseline are the edge files now being read; proofs unchanged, R190 still proved by its server test.
- Manual probe: temporary `apps/edge/src/__probe2828__.ts` holding a bogus R-id failed the check with `apps/edge/src/__probe2828__.ts:1: R999999 has no note in spec/rulings/`; removed afterwards and the tree checks clean.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge` — 19 passed, including the two untouched `R190` titles.

## Decisions and departures from the plan

- The plan assumed `check()`'s error message would name the offending path; it does not — problems print to stdout and the error carries only the count. The test asserts the count (`spec check: 1 problem(s)`) on a tree identical to the passing one except the edge file, plus a restore-to-valid control, which pins causality in both directions.
- Same-sentence fix beyond the plan's two quoted edits: "those three trees" became "those four trees", otherwise the sentence would contradict the code.
- Rejected alternative (forbidding R-citations in edge): edge already cites R190, so forbidding would mean rewriting those comments — bigger and against the grain.
- Left for a possible follow-up: `CLAUDE.md` rule 3 still lists the old three roots. It was out of the issue's two-file scope, so I did not touch it.

### Adversarial review

Approved on round 1 of 3.

Notes the reviewer left (not blocking):

- `CLAUDE.md:40`: Rule 3 still lists only crates/, apps/web/src/ and e2e/ as the checked trees, so it now understates the check's four roots.

# #2828: Patch: spec check reads the edge worker's ruling citations too
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Ruling references written in code comments are machine-checked against the spec's ruling notes, so a typo fails loudly instead of rotting. Today that safety net skips the edge worker at the login and rate-limit boundary. After this change the same net covers it, so a wrong ruling number there fails the check like everywhere else.
## Why
`CITING_ROOTS` in `crates/tools/src/spec.rs` is exactly `crates`, `apps/web/src` and `e2e`, yet `apps/edge/src/routing.ts` cites R190 in a comment and `apps/edge/src/routing.test.ts` holds `R190` tests. And `spec/README.md` counts a proving test only under `apps/web` or `e2e`, so an edge test can never satisfy a note's `proven_in`. Both directions are unchecked: a mistyped R-id in edge passes silently, and a ruling proved only in edge looks unproved.
## Proposal
Extend the check's citing roots and proving-test rule to `apps/edge/src` (the smallest reading), or forbid R-citations there if the maintainer prefers edge to stay citation-free; either way update `spec/README.md` so the documented rule matches the code. No behavior change to the game.
## Where it lands
Files: `crates/tools/src/spec.rs` (`CITING_ROOTS`, the proving-test matcher), `spec/README.md` (Adding a ruling, proving-test rule). Touched but unchanged in meaning: `apps/edge/src/routing.ts`, `spec/rulings/R0190.md`. SPEC sections: §9.4, R190.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` passes on a clean tree.
- [ ] A probe with a bogus R-id under `apps/edge` fails the check (temporary fixture, removed afterwards).
- [ ] R190 still resolves and its edge tests still run; the README rule matches the new behavior.
## Size and risks
Small work, suggested `difficulty:medium` (tooling plus a spec doc). Risk is a newly-surfaced pre-existing typo in edge failing the check; that is the point, and the fix is to correct the citation.

In the final paragraph (~line 59), change "an `R<n>` cited anywhere in `crates/`, `apps/web/src/` or `e2e/`" to "…in `crates/`, `apps/web/src/`, `apps/edge/src/` or `e2e/`". No other wording changes.
5. Do not take the alternative design (forbidding R-citations in edge): edge already cites R190 in a comment and two test titles, so forbidding would mean rewriting those comments — bigger and against the grain.

## Tests

- New: `check_reads_edge_workers_citations` in `crates/tools/src/spec.rs` (`mod tests`) — asserts a valid edge citation passes the check, a bogus R-id under `apps/edge/src` fails naming that path, and an edge TS title proves its ruling. Fails without step 1 (bogus id passes silently); passes with it. Run: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools spec::tests::check_reads_edge_workers_citations` then the full module: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools spec`.
- Existing edge suite (must still run, unchanged): `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge` (the two `R190` titles in `apps/edge/src/routing.test.ts`).
- Checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check` (clean tree must pass; then a manual probe — temporary file under `apps/edge/src/` with a bogus R-id, e.g. `// R999999 probe`, confirming the check fails naming it, removed afterwards; the new unit test automates the same probe permanently).

## Done when

- [ ] `CITING_ROOTS` includes `apps/edge/src` and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes on a clean tree.
- [ ] A bogus R-id probe under `apps/edge` fails the check (unit test green; manual temporary-fixture probe done and removed).
- [ ] R190 still resolves, `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge` passes, and the README rule matches the new behavior in both sentences.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools spec`, fmt and clippy gates above are green; no file outside the two listed changed.

## Risks

- A pre-existing typo'd R-id under `apps/edge/src` may newly fail the check — that is the point; fix the citation, never narrow the roots.
- `spec.rs` is itself walked by rule 3: any literal bogus R-id added in the new test's source would fail the real check, which is why step 3 builds it with `format!`. Likewise keep added test names free of `r<n>` tokens and cite only R1/R3.
- `proves()` dispatches on file extension only, with no path-prefix guard — no code change needed on the proving side; the README sentence is the fix there. Do not add a path guard (unrequested behavior change that could reject legitimate proofs).

## Open questions

None. No person-only step: everything is outside `.github/`, `.harness/`, `bot/`, needs no secret or dashboard, and the maintainer's approve comment already chose the covering-edge direction over the citation-free alternative.

Baseline confirmed: `cargo jackioh spec check` passes on the clean tree — `spec check: 1625 rulings, 3848 proofs, 47607 citations in 3103 files, 20634 links: ok`. The plan above stands unchanged; the draft in `.bot-plan.md` now records this result (plus a note that the release build took ~36 minutes, so the builder should reuse the built binary).
